# Pocock's artifacts live in the existing tables: spec, map and capability as scoped documents;…

Pocock's artifacts live in the existing tables: spec, map and capability as scoped documents; project and out-of-scope as repo documents; delta on sections; ticket type and blockers on tasks; gates as decision records

Why: the sync plugin reads the kinds and fields from Imprimatur's lists (DOC_KINDS, FIELDS, CHAPTERS), so new kinds in the same tables sync with small changes instead of a new sync entity.

- documents.kind adds spec, map, capability (scoped: a task's key, a capability's name) and project, out-of-scope (one per repo). The scope rule is now "scoped kinds have a scope". Old kinds stay until #185 moves their content.
- CHAPTERS: spec = Pocock's to-spec sections; map = destination, notes, decisions, fog, out-of-scope; project = mission, constraints, stack, roadmap.
- doc_sections.delta (added, modified, removed, renamed), only on a spec's sections: OpenSpec's change to a capability.
- tasks.ticket_type (research, prototype, grilling, task) and tasks.blocked_by (JSON list of keys): tickets are tasks.
- Kiro's gates and the analyze step are decision records with links.gate: no schema.
- Sync (imprimatur-private): sync key "<kind>:<scope>" for every scoped kind ("analysis:<key>" unchanged), new task and section fields validated.

Migration 16 ran on a copy of the real database (all counts equal, integrity ok, 10 ms). Note: it also ran on the real database as soon as the branch's code was on disk, because the hooks load this checkout.
